Title: A feed you can inspect
Description: Why a generated feed should remain understandable without a feed reader.
Author: Mara Bell
Body:
An RSS feed is most useful when its source stays boring. Open `feed.xml` here and the channel, dates, links, and categories are all visible.

SMGen builds the file with XMLWriter. The template only marks this row for the `notes` feed.

Title: Keeping an archive static
Description: Building useful archive navigation without shipping a browser application.
Author: Mara Bell
Body:
The calendar and year groups are generated before deployment. Native `details` elements handle expansion, so the archive works before any script could run.

The same publication date places this post in the calendar, timeline, feed, sitemap, and structured data.

Title: Shipping fewer browser assets
Description: How page selection keeps feature assets away from pages that do not need them.
Author: Ilan Reed
Body:
A feature should pay its way on the page that uses it. SMGen adds the archive stylesheet because this site places a populated timeline in the sidebar.

There is no archive script. Sites without a timeline do not request the archive stylesheet.

Title: Turning rows into posts
Description: A short data-page template can supply content and publication metadata together.
Author: Ilan Reed
Body:
The CSV holds the prose and fields an editor changes. A trusted PHP template converts each selected row into Markdown and YAML frontmatter.

Local validation catches missing columns, duplicate slugs, malformed rows, and unsafe output paths before the site build begins.

Title: One build and three outputs
Description: One publication date can drive a page archive and feed item.
Author: Mara Bell
Body:
The page is the first output visitors see. The same source also contributes an entry to the archive and an item to the RSS feed.

Those outputs share a date because the template writes it once. No browser code joins them after deployment.

Title: Starting with plain files
Description: The first version of the example needed a spreadsheet and two small templates.
Author: Ilan Reed
Body:
The source of this blog is a CSV file beside its templates. A normal SMGen build produces HTML, XML, navigation data, and a sitemap.

The published directory can move to GitHub Pages, object storage, or any host that serves static files.
